# Founder report: Monthly Bitcoin Cash sticker box, location unspecified

## Executive summary

The idea is a $25 monthly box of Bitcoin Cash (BCH, a small cryptocurrency) stickers and merch for people who attend meetups. The strongest evidence for it is that about 30% of U.S. adults owned crypto heading into 2026 [S1], and BCH still has about 2,572 merchants accepting it [S2]. The strongest evidence against it is price: a three-sticker BCH set sells for $4.99, about $1.66 per sticker [S7], so $25 buys about 15 stickers at that rate. Only 11% of surveyed U.S. adults planned to buy BCH in the next 12 months, against 59% for Bitcoin [S1]. The research found no city, meetup attendance count, or merch buyer data, so demand is unproven. Using estimated costs, each subscriber brings in about €10.55 a month after variable costs, and the business needs 13 subscribers to cover €130 of monthly fixed costs. Startup capital is estimated at €950. Those break-even figures rest on estimates, not sourced costs. Verdict: Test first (score 3.0/10). Main reason: The case is open because the idea names no location, and the research found no meetup attendance, merch buyer or subscription-box price data for any city. No sourced evidence rules it out, so test the open points before you commit savings.

## Verdict

**TEST FIRST** (score 3.0/10)

- The case is open because the idea names no location, and the research found no meetup attendance, merch buyer or subscription-box price data for any city.
- The price is the main sourced concern. Single-seller BCH stickers cost about $1.66 each [S7][S8][S9], and a $25 box needs a clear reason to cost about five times a $4.99 three-pack [S7].
- Demand signals are weak but not negative. Crypto ownership is near 30% [S1], BCH still has about 2,572 accepting merchants [S2], and 65% of forum users back wider BCH acceptance [S5]. The forum figure comes from forum posts, not a sampled survey.
- Subscription churn (customers cancelling each month) is high for this kind of box. General boxes run 10–15% a month [S15], and 44% of cancellations happen in the first 90 days [S18]. A pre-sale test can show whether buyers stay.

## 3 things to validate first

1. **Meetup attendees will pay $25 a month in advance for a box of BCH stickers and merch.**
    - *Why it matters:* If no one pre-orders at $25, the box has no buyers, and the rest of the plan has no basis.
    - *Test this month:* Show a $25 pre-order page to attendees at two meetups or in one online BCH group. Run it for four weeks, and log every person who sees the offer and every person who pays.
    - *Pass:* At least 13 prepaid subscribers from the first 60 people who see the offer.

2. **Contents can be bought for less than €12.45 landed (delivered) per box.**
    - *Why it matters:* If stickers and merch cost more to source, the margin shown in the unit economics disappears, and the box loses money on every shipment.
    - *Test this month:* Get written quotes from at least two sticker printers and one apparel supplier for 15 stickers and one merch item in a 30-unit run. Include delivery to you.
    - *Pass:* Quoted contents cost no more than €6 per box (estimate), before packaging and postage.

3. **Subscribers stay past the first 90 days.**
    - *Why it matters:* Most cancellations happen early [S18]. If the box loses people in months one to three, each subscriber is worth much less than the break-even model assumes.
    - *Test this month:* Run a three-month pilot with at least 20 pre-order subscribers. Track cancellations, failed card payments, and reasons given.
    - *Pass:* Monthly cancellations stay under 10% [S15], and at most 4 of the first 20 subscribers leave within 90 days.

## Customers & demand

**Takeaway:** Crypto ownership is high enough to find buyers, but BCH intent is low. There is no sourced evidence of demand for a $25 monthly box in any city, so the case rests on the pre-order test.

**Evidence:**
- (+) About 30% of U.S. adults owned crypto heading into 2026, helped by spot Bitcoin ETF (exchange-traded fund, a fund that holds bitcoin and trades like a stock) approval [S1].
- (−) Only 11% of the same U.S. adults said they planned to buy BCH in the next 12 months, against 59% for Bitcoin [S1].
- (+) About 2,572 businesses accepted BCH in mid-2026, per a Cryptwerk merchant database [S2]. That source is an AI-generated price-forecast page, so treat it as lower confidence. An earlier figure of 2,476 merchants [S3] suggests modest growth, but the dates conflict.
- (−) Daily BCH transactions are disputed: about 150,000, up 40% from 2023 [S4], versus about 10,000–15,000 [S2]. Online gambling is named as a main driver of volume [S6], which may not reflect merch buyers.
- (+) 65% of community users back wider BCH acceptance as a payment method [S5]. This comes from forum posts, not a sampled survey.
- (?) No city, neighbourhood or population was named, so no local buyer count could be found. No meetup attendance figures were found for any city.
- (?) No household spending data on crypto collectibles or novelty subscription boxes was found.

**Key numbers:**

| Figure | Value | Source or "estimate" |
|---|---|---|
| U.S. adults owning crypto, heading into 2026 | About 30% | S1 |
| U.S. adults planning to buy BCH in 12 months | 11% | S1 |
| U.S. adults planning to buy Bitcoin in 12 months | 59% | S1 |
| BCH merchants accepting payment, mid-2026 | About 2,572 | S2 (lower confidence) |
| Community users backing wider BCH acceptance | 65% | S5 (forum posts) |
| Daily BCH transactions | 10,000–15,000 or about 150,000 (disputed) | S2, S4 |

**What it means for you:** Your buyers are most likely people already inside the BCH community, not crypto owners in general. The 11% BCH purchase intent [S1] suggests the pool is small, so the pre-order test should target people who already attend BCH events. Do not assume the broad crypto ownership figure applies to your customers.

**Next actions:**
1. Pick the meetup or online group you will test in, and write down its size and how often it meets.
2. Post a short survey asking attendees how much they would pay monthly for a sticker and merch box, with $10, $25 and $40 options.
3. Count how many people in the group already own BCH merch, and ask what they bought and where.

## Competition & alternatives

**Takeaway:** The cheapest BCH stickers cost about $1.66 each, so a $25 box must justify its price with merch or exclusivity. No BCH subscription box or meetup merch subscription was found.

**Evidence:**
- (−) The official BCH sticker seller sells three 3-inch logo stickers for $4.99, with free worldwide shipping [S7]. That is about $1.66 per sticker, and the seller says the stickers are weatherproof [S7].
- (−) Independent Redbubble designers list BCH stickers from $1.66 to about $1.98 [S8][S9], and another BCH sticker listing starts at $1.79 [S13]. The Etsy listing for a BCH vinyl sticker is $3.00 [S11].
- (=) Redbubble and TeePublic both sell BCH shirts and sticker designs [S10][S14], but no shirt or sticker prices were captured for TeePublic, and no apparel unit prices were found on Redbubble.
- (?) No BCH-specific subscription box or meetup merch subscription was found. The search does not prove none exists, because it covered only one search.
- (?) No local sellers, meetup merch prices or print-shop prices were found, because no city was named.

**Key numbers:**

| Figure | Value | Source or "estimate" |
|---|---|---|
| BCH sticker set, three stickers | $4.99 | S7 |
| Cost per sticker, single seller | About $1.66 | S7 (calculated) |
| Redbubble BCH sticker, from | $1.66–$1.98 | S8, S9 |
| Redbubble BCH "Accepted Here" sticker, from | $1.79 | S13 |
| Etsy BCH vinyl sticker | $3.00 | S11 |
| Stickers that $25 buys at $1.67 each | About 15 | Estimate |

**What it means for you:** A $25 box would be a poor deal for stickers alone, since $25 buys about 15 stickers at the single-seller rate. The box needs merch that is clearly worth more, or a reason for buyers to pay for regular delivery, such as early access to limited designs. Test whether buyers value that extra, or whether they would rather buy stickers one-off at about $5 to $10.

**Next actions:**
1. Order the $4.99 sticker set from the official seller to check quality, weatherproofing and delivery time against your planned product.
2. Search for BCH sellers in the city or region where you plan to test, and record their prices and whether they sell at meetups.
3. Write down the one reason a buyer would pay $25 rather than $5 to $10 for one-off stickers, and test it in the pre-order survey.

## Money

**Takeaway:** At $25 a month, the box can cover its estimated costs if it reaches the break-even subscriber count. The cost inputs are estimates because the research found no supplier costs, rent, wages or local tax figures.

**Evidence:**
- (+) The idea price is $25 a month. The research found no subscription box at that price, so it is not directly compared with other boxes.
- (=) Retail prices for single items are low. A BCH vinyl sticker is $3.00 on Etsy [S11], and a 25-pack of Bitcoin stickers is $8.10 [S11].
- (−) Average subscription box prices in 2026 are $43–$47 [S16], so $25 sits well below the average. This could help a first-time box attract buyers, but it also means less room in the price for merch.
- (−) Payment failures on monthly charges run about 7–12% [S21]. Each failed charge is a lost payment unless a retry tool recovers it, which adds a cost.
- (?) No sticker, vinyl, blank or print cost was found. No shipping rate, packaging cost or payment fee was found.
- (?) No VAT rate was found, because no country was named. The unit economics below therefore show no VAT.
- (?) No commercial rent, trade wages or employer social security figures were found, because no city was named.

**Key numbers:**

| Figure | Value | Source or "estimate" |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly price, idea | $25 (about €23 at an assumed 0.92 EUR per USD) | Idea; exchange rate is an estimate |
| Three BCH stickers | $4.99 | S7 |
| Stickers per $25 box at single-seller rate | About 15 | Estimate |
| Average subscription box price, 2026 | $43–$47 | S16 |
| Payment failure rate on monthly dues | 7–12% | S21 |
| Startup capital | €950 | Estimate |
| Fixed monthly costs | €130 | Estimate |
| Break-even | 13 subscribers | Estimate |

**Unit economics**

The model uses one subscriber-month as the unit of sale. The customer pays $25, which is about €23 at an estimated rate of 0.92 EUR per USD. No VAT is included, because no country was named. The business keeps the full net price, since it sells directly.

Variable costs per subscriber-month are estimates: contents (stickers and merch) about €6, packaging about €1.50, postage about €4.00, and payment fees about €0.95. Those costs add up to €12.45. After them, each subscriber contributes €10.55, a contribution margin of 46%%.

Fixed monthly costs are estimates: subscription management software about €35, accounting about €30, liability insurance about €25, and storage about €40. Together they total €130. Dividing fixed costs by contribution per subscriber gives the break-even count of 13 subscribers. Startup capital of €950 covers design, a sample print run, a checkout page and registration. The owner's pay is not included, so the model shows the box covering its own costs, not a salary.

**What it means for you:** The box needs about 13 paying subscribers before it covers its estimated monthly costs. That is a small number, but it assumes contents cost about €6 per box, which is unverified. Your savings are at risk until the supplier quotes and pre-order results are in. Do not commit more than the startup capital to stock until both are known.

**Next actions:**
1. Get two printer quotes and one apparel quote for a 30-unit run, and replace the estimated contents cost with the quoted figure.
2. Compare the software and payment fees of two subscription platforms, and check which one retries failed payments.
3. Check with a local accountant or tax office what registration, VAT and insurance are required in your country, and update the fixed costs.

## Risks & how to start

**Takeaway:** Subscription churn, failed payments and platform dependency are the main risks. The research found no subscription-box failure rates, so the business failure figure used here is a general small-business estimate.

**Evidence:**
- (−) General subscription boxes lose 10–15% of subscribers a month [S15]. Curated lifestyle boxes lose 7–10% [S16], and top performers stay under 3% [S16].
- (−) 44% of subscription box cancellations happen in the first 90 days [S18]. First-month churn runs 15–25% across categories [S17].
- (−) Raising a $60 box to $66 pushed churn from 6% to a range of 7–9% [S17]. Price increases are a risk if merch costs rise.
- (=) Sources disagree on involuntary churn (cancellations caused by failed payments, not customer choice). One source says 68% [S19], another says 25–35% [S20]. Plan for both: a retry tool and a clear payment update process.
- (=) Platform churn tracks merchant churn, so a software platform that loses its merchants may also lose its ability to run your box [S22].
- (=) Business closure rates are about 20% in year one and 50% by year five for U.S. small businesses, cited from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS, the U.S. federal labour statistics agency) via a secondary site [S16]. The figures were not checked against BLS directly, and no subscription-box failure rate was found.
- (?) No local permits, business registration, self-employment costs, market stall fees or shared-kitchen prices were found, because no city was named.
- (?) No pre-sale or sticker-only test data was found.

**Key numbers:**

| Figure | Value | Source or "estimate" |
|---|---|---|
| General subscription box churn, monthly | 10–15% | S15 |
| Curated lifestyle box churn, monthly | 7–10% | S16 |
| Cancellations within first 90 days | 44% | S18 |
| First-month churn | 15–25% | S17 |
| Payment failure rate on monthly dues | 7–12% | S21 |
| U.S. small-business closures, year one | About 20% (secondary source) | S16 |

**What it means for you:** Most of the risk comes from subscribers leaving early and from failed payments, not from the stickers. A monthly box is hard to keep going if the first three months lose many people. Keep your startup spending small until the pre-order test shows buyers will stay. Do not sign a platform contract until you know how it handles failed payments.

**Next actions:**
1. Choose a payment platform that includes failed-payment retries, and ask it for its own monthly churn figure.
2. Run a sticker-only pre-order, with no monthly commitment, to test interest before building the subscription.
3. Check which registrations, permits and insurance your city or country requires for selling goods online and at events, and write them into the fixed costs.
